content.text:
Explore the thos codebase to understand the architecture for adding a diff viewer feature. I need to understand:

1. How the dashboard currently displays messages and tool results (especially file edits/writes)
2. The message types and structures in lib/types.ts - particularly anything related to file operations (Edit, Write, etc.)
3. How components in components/dashboard/ render different types of content
4. How the condensed-tool-group.tsx works (it likely groups tool calls)
5. The current message rendering flow from use-websocket.ts → page → components

Focus on understanding what data is available about file diffs/edits and how they're currently displayed. Look at the message component, chat component, and any tool-result rendering logic.

   113→## 2026-02-17 — Fix duplicate "Session started" on follow-up messages

   123→## 2026-02-17 — Fix message duplication in chat
   124→
   125→Claude CLI sends cumulative NDJSON snapshots for assistant messages (each line is a complete snapshot of the message so far). The server correctly deduplicates these in stored history, but the browser received every snapshot as a live relay and appended each one as a new ChatMessage, causing messages to appear 2-4x in the chat window. Also caused React duplicate key warnings.

Changed `relayChatMessage()` to use these stable IDs (prefixed with `dedup-`) instead of generating new random IDs for each snapshot. Updated the relay handler to replace existing ChatMessages with the same dedup ID instead of appending. Added `findLastRawIndex()` helper to also deduplicate raw messages in the debug view.

1→# thos
     2→
     3→**the orchestrator you never knew you needed**
     4→
     5→A visual orchestration layer for [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code). Not another IDE — a UI that sits on top of the terminal-based agents you already use, solving the real friction of working with them day-to-day.
     6→
     7→## The Problem
     8→
     9→AI coding agents are powerful, but the experience of *using* them has real gaps:
    10→
    11→- **You lose track of what's happening.** Multiple agents running across tasks, and you're tab-switching and scrolling terminals to figure out who's doing what. The visibility problem compounds fast.
    12→
    13→- **Agents are smart but have the memory of an infant.** Your workflows are specific to you — your project structure, your preferences, your domain knowledge. The agent doesn't retain any of it between sessions. You end up re-explaining the same context over and over. A static CLAUDE.md helps, but it doesn't learn from your conversations or evolve with your codebase.
    14→
    15→- **Your machine is the bottleneck.** You have a laptop, not a build server. Agents want to compile, test, run — and your local machine can't keep up.
    16→
    17→- **Undoing things is painful.** Agent makes a wrong turn, and now you're doing forensics. Better change tracking, rollback, and context management should be table stakes — not an afterthought.
    18→
    19→- **Task management is manual.** Coordinating what gets done, in what order, across which agents — that's on you, in your head, with no tooling to help.
    20→
    21→## What thos Is
    22→
    23→thos is a UI wrapper around Claude Code. Terminals are fine — but when you're orchestrating work across agents, you need something more visual.
    24→
    25→Think of it as a control plane:
    26→
    27→- **Agent dashboard** — see what every agent is doing, in real time, at a glance
    28→- **Persistent memory** — agents that learn from your conversations and retain domain knowledge across sessions. Not just saved prompts — context that evolves with your codebase and workflows, so the first time you explain something is the last time.
    29→- **Change management** — track, diff, and roll back agent-generated changes with confidence
    30→- **Task orchestration** — assign, sequence, and track work across agents
    31→- **Remote access** — web UI accessible via localhost, with the option to expose over your network as needed
    32→
    33→## What thos Is Not
    34→
    35→- **Not an IDE.** VS Code, Cursor, Zed — these are well-engineered. thos doesn't compete with them; it complements them.
    36→- **Not a terminal replacement.** The terminal is the execution layer. thos is the visibility and coordination layer on top.
    37→- **Not a general agent framework.** Focused on Claude Code first. Breadth comes later, if it makes sense.
    38→
    39→## Prior Art
    40→
    41→Similar space as [superset.sh](https://superset.sh) and [Conductor](https://conductor.sh) — tools that recognize the gap between raw agent capability and the UX of actually orchestrating agent work.
    42→
    43→## Architecture
    44→
    45→### WebSocket relay server (`server/ws.ts`)
    46→
    47→A standalone WebSocket server on port 9900, started alongside Next.js via `concurrently`. Two connection families:
    48→
    49→- **`/browser`** — React dashboard connects here. Supports multiple tabs simultaneously.
    50→- **`/claude/:agentId`** — each Claude CLI connects here (passed as `--sdk-url`).
    51→
    52→The server acts as a relay: browser spawns agents, the server launches `claude` inside tmux sessions, and all CLI NDJSON messages are forwarded to the browser as `{ type: "relay", agentId, message }`.
    53→
    54→### Session persistence (`server/session-store.ts`)
    55→
    56→Agent state and full message history are persisted to `$TMPDIR/thos-sessions/<agentId>.json`. This means:
    57→
    58→- **Page refresh** restores all conversations — the server replays `message_history` to each connecting browser.
    59→- **Server restart** restores agents from disk. On startup, the server checks which tmux sessions are still alive (`tmux list-sessions`) and marks agents accordingly — `disconnected` if the tmux session survived, `done` if it didn't.
    60→- **Multiple browser tabs** see the same state — `sendToBrowser` iterates a `Set<WebSocket>` of all connected browsers.
    61→
    62→Writes are **debounced** (150ms) for high-frequency streaming events and **synchronous** for critical state changes (spawn, result, status transitions). On `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`, all agents are flushed to disk. **Tmux sessions are intentionally preserved** — they survive server restarts and shutdowns, so a quick server bounce doesn't destroy running CLI processes.
    63→
    64→### CLI resilience
    65→
    66→| Scenario | Behavior |
    67→|----------|----------|
    68→| CLI process exits or crashes | Status becomes `"done"`, agent moves to the Archived section in the sidebar. Browser sees "CLI session ended". |
    69→| Server restarts | Agents restored from disk. Tmux sessions are preserved — if a session is still alive, the agent is marked `"disconnected"`; otherwise `"done"`. |
    70→| Message sent while CLI is down | Queued in `pendingMessages[]`, flushed if/when the CLI WebSocket reconnects |
    71→| CLI reconnects (manual) | Browser sees "CLI reconnected", queued messages are delivered |
    72→
    73→> **Note:** Claude CLI's `--resume` flag does not reliably reconnect to a previous `--sdk-url` conversation, so automatic relaunch was removed. Ended agents are archived as read-only.
    74→
    75→### Agent status lifecycle
    76→
    77→```
    78→idle → spawning → connected ⇄ thinking → done
    79→                                           ↑
    80→                 disconnected ─────────────┘ (CLI exit/crash)
    81→                      │
    82→                    error
    83→```
    84→
    85→- `idle` — no process, ready to spawn
    86→- `spawning` — tmux session created, waiting for CLI WebSocket
    87→- `connected` — CLI connected, `system/init` received
    88→- `thinking` — waiting for assistant response
    89→- `done` — CLI finished or disconnected (terminal state)
    90→- `disconnected` — restored from disk with a live tmux session but no CLI WebSocket
    91→- `error` — unrecoverable failure
    92→
    93→Agents with status `done`, `disconnected`, or `error` are **archived** — they appear in a separate sidebar section and their chat is read-only ("This session has ended").
    94→
    95→### Message flow
    96→
    97→```
    98→Browser                    WS Server                    Claude CLI
    99→  │                           │                            │
   100→  │──spawn(prompt)──────────▶│                            │
   101→  │                           │──tmux new-session──────▶│
   102→  │◀──spawned(agentId)───────│                            │
   103→  │                           │◀──hook_response───────────│
   104→  │                           │──user(prompt)────────────▶│
   105→  │◀──relay(system/init)─────│◀──system/init──────────────│
   106→  │◀──relay(assistant)───────│◀──assistant─────────────────│
   107→  │◀──relay(control_request)─│◀──control_request──────────│
   108→  │──control_response───────▶│──control_response─────────▶│
   109→  │◀──relay(result)──────────│◀──result────────────────────│
   110→  │                           │                            │
   111→  │  (page refresh)           │                            │
   112→  │──connect /browser────────▶│                            │
   113→  │◀──agent_list─────────────│                            │
   114→  │◀──message_history────────│  (replays all stored msgs) │
   115→```
   116→
   117→### Agent management
   118→
   119→Right-click (or click the kebab icon) on any agent in the sidebar to open a context menu:
   120→
   121→| Action | When available | What it does |
   122→|--------|---------------|--------------|
   123→| **Rename** | Always | Swaps the label for an inline input (Enter to confirm, Escape to cancel) |
   124→| **Kill** | `spawning`, `connected`, `thinking` | Kills the tmux session + CLI WebSocket, sets status to `"done"` — agent moves to Archived |
   125→| **Clear History** | Always | Wipes the agent's message history on server and all connected browsers |
   126→| **Delete** | Always | Confirmation prompt, then permanently removes the agent from the Map, disk, and sidebar |
   127→
   128→The sidebar is split into two sections:
   129→- **Active** — agents with status `spawning`, `connected`, or `thinking`
   130→- **Archived** — agents with status `done`, `disconnected`, or `error` (rendered with muted styling, chat is read-only)
   131→
   132→The full round-trip for each action: browser sends a typed message (e.g. `kill_agent`), the server performs the operation and broadcasts updated state, all connected browsers reconcile.
   133→
   134→### Claude NDJSON snapshot deduplication
   135→
   136→Claude Code's `--sdk-url` WebSocket emits NDJSON messages. Two message types — `assistant` and `user` — are sent as **cumulative snapshots**: each NDJSON line contains the full `message.content` array up to that point, not just the delta. This means if an assistant response has 100 content blocks, the CLI emits 100 messages, each one a superset of the previous. The same applies to `user` messages carrying `tool_result` blocks — every tool invocation triggers a new cumulative snapshot of all tool results so far.
   137→
   138→Without deduplication, storing every snapshot produces **O(n²) storage**. A real-world session with 75 assistant turns and ~130 tool calls generated:
   139→
   140→```
   141→Total messages stored:     8,893
   142→Unique (after dedup):        208
   143→File size before:           38 MB
   144→File size after:            ~1 MB
   145→```
   146→
   147→**How dedup works:**
   148→
   149→Each snapshot message has a stable `message.id` field. The `recordAndSend` function in `server/ws.ts` checks whether the last entry in `messageHistory` with the same `message.id` already exists. If so, it **replaces** that entry instead of appending. This keeps only the final version of each message.
   150→
   151→```
   152→CLI sends:  assistant(id=abc, content=[block1])
   153→            assistant(id=abc, content=[block1, block2])
   154→            assistant(id=abc, content=[block1, block2, block3])
   155→
   156→Stored:     assistant(id=abc, content=[block1, block2, block3])   ← only the final snapshot
   157→```
   158→
   159→Live relay to the browser is unaffected — all intermediate snapshots are still streamed in real time for smooth rendering. The deduplication only applies to what gets persisted in `messageHistory` and written to disk.
   160→
   161→**Compaction on startup:**
   162→
   163→Old session files written before dedup was added are compacted on server restore. `compactHistory()` scans the full history, identifies duplicate message IDs, and keeps only the last occurrence. The compacted version is immediately persisted back to disk, so the file shrinks on the next server start.
   164→
   165→### Network access
   166→
   167→The WebSocket server and Next.js frontend bind to `0.0.0.0` (all interfaces) but restrict connections to **localhost** and **Tailscale IPs** (100.64.0.0/10 CGNAT range). Non-allowed IPs are rejected at the application layer:
   168→
   169→- **WS server** — `verifyClient` callback checks `req.socket.remoteAddress` before accepting the WebSocket upgrade.
   170→- **Next.js** — `middleware.ts` checks the request IP and returns 403 for disallowed sources.
   171→
   172→The `WS_URL` in the React hook is derived from `window.location.hostname` rather than hardcoded to `localhost`, so the dashboard works from any allowed host (e.g. `http://100.x.x.x:3000`).
   173→
   174→### Lazy history loading
   175→
   176→Message histories are **not** sent eagerly on browser connect. The initial payload contains only `agent_list` (sidebar metadata) and `task_list` — both small. When the user selects an agent, the browser sends `{ type: "request_history", agentId }` and the server responds with that agent's `message_history`. Previously viewed agents are cached client-side (`loadedAgents` Set) so switching back is instant.
   177→
   178→This avoids sending megabytes of JSON on connect, which matters on slower networks and when many agents have large histories.
   179→
   180→### Raw message viewer
   181→
   182→A `raw` toggle in the top-right corner of the chat status bar switches between the processed chat view and a debug view showing every raw Claude NDJSON message. Each message row is collapsible and color-coded by type (`system` yellow, `assistant` blue, `result` green, `control_request` orange).
   183→
   184→### Key files
   185→
   186→| File | Purpose |
   187→|------|---------|
   188→| `server/ws.ts` | WebSocket relay server — agent lifecycle, message routing, multi-browser, persistence integration |
   189→| `server/session-store.ts` | File-based JSON persistence with debounced/sync writes |
   190→| `hooks/use-websocket.ts` | React hook — connection management, message processing, dedup, reconnect handling |
   191→| `lib/types.ts` | Shared TypeScript types for all message protocols |
   192→| `components/dashboard/agent-sidebar.tsx` | Agent list with status dots, right-click context menu, inline rename |
   193→| `components/dashboard/chat.tsx` | Chat interface with raw message debug viewer |
   194→| `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx` | Connection and agent status indicator |
   195→
   196→## Status
   197→
   198→Early stage. Solving my own problems first, seeing where it goes from there.
   199→
   200→---
   201→
   202→Built by [@chiumax](https://github.com/chiumax)
   203→

## Research Summary: Integrating diffs.com into thos

I've completed a thorough analysis of the thos codebase for diffs.com integration. Here are my findings:

### 1. **Existing diffs.com Reference**
- Found in `.thos/tasks/tasks.json` (ID: `1e8543f8`):
  - **Title:** "diff viewer"
  - **Description:** "want to view diffs of files\nuse https://diffs.com/"
  - **Status:** "in-progress"
  - **Priority:** "medium"
  - **Linked Agent:** `125b84f5`
  - This is an active task already tracked in the system

### 2. **Current Link Handling in the UI**

**Markdown Rendering:**
- The codebase uses `react-markdown` with `remark-gfm` (GitHub Flavored Markdown)
- Located in `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/components/dashboard/message.tsx` (line 109)
- Assistant messages render markdown; user messages remain plain text
- Links are styled via `.prose-msg a` in `app/globals.css` (lines 212-215):
  ```css
  .prose-msg a {
    color: oklch(0.75 0.18 55);
    text-decoration: underline;
  }
  ```

**Current Link Behavior:**
- Links in markdown render as simple `<a>` elements with href attributes
- No special handling for external resources or iframes
- Links open in the default browser behavior (same tab)

### 3. **No Existing iframe or Embedded Content Patterns**

**Search Results:**
- No existing iframe implementations found in the codebase
- No embedded content widgets currently used
- The application focuses on terminal I/O, messages, and control requests
- All external resources are mentioned as text links within markdown

### 4. **Package.json Dependencies Analysis**

**Relevant packages:**
- `react-markdown` (v10.1.0) — for markdown parsing
- `remark-gfm` (v4.0.1) — GitHub Flavored Markdown support
- `ws` (v8.19.0) — WebSocket server

**Notable absences:**
- No diff-viewing library (diff2html, react-diff-view, etc.)
- No iframe-related libraries
- No external URL handling utilities

### 5. **Architecture Considerations**

**For diffs.com Integration:**

**Option A: Direct Link (Current)**
- Users click markdown links to `https://diffs.com/...`
- Already works; files just need to be formatted with diffs.com links

**Option B: Embed/Component Integration**
- Would require custom React component
- Could add iframe support with proper security headers
- Needs CSP (Content Security Policy) configuration

**Option C: File Upload to diffs.com**
- Would need API integration
- Could automatically POST file contents when changes are detected
- Requires adding fetch/axios and handling API responses

### 6. **Existing Message and Content Handling**

**Message Component Flow:**
```
app/dashboard/page.tsx 
  → Chat component
    → Message component (renders markdown)
      → react-markdown with remark-gfm plugin
        → Outputs HTML including <a> tags
```

**Control/Tool Request Handling:**
- `control-request.tsx` displays tool inputs/outputs with code blocks
- Already handles rich content display (scrollable code, formatted parameters)
- Uses custom styling for different content types

### 7. **Relevant File Locations**

| File | Purpose | Relevant for diffs.com |
|------|---------|------------------------|
| `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/components/dashboard/message.tsx` | Message rendering with markdown | Main integration point |
| `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/app/globals.css` | All CSS including `.prose-msg a` | Link styling |
| `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/lib/types.ts` | Type definitions for messages | May need message type updates |
| `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/hooks/use-websocket.ts` | Message processing logic | Could detect and transform diff URLs |
| `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/components/dashboard/control-request.tsx` | Tool result display | Reference for rich content patterns |
| `/Users/chiu.fyi/thos/package.json` | Dependencies | Add new packages if needed |

### 8. **Key Integration Points**

**If embedding diffs.com inline:**
1. Extend `ChatMessage` type in `lib/types.ts` to support diff metadata
2. Create custom React component for diff viewer (iframe or API-based)
3. Modify message rendering in `components/dashboard/message.tsx`
4. Add security headers for iframe embedding

**If generating shareable diffs.com links:**
1. Add URL generation logic in `hooks/use-websocket.ts` when processing file changes
2. Transform file paths into diffs.com shareable URLs
3. Render as markdown links (already supported)

**If creating a diff panel widget:**
1. Similar to `TaskPanel` pattern in `kanban-board.tsx`
2. Add new modal/drawer component
3. Wire through to dashboard page layout

### 9. **Security & CSP Considerations**

The application currently has:
- IP-based access control (localhost + Tailscale) in `middleware.ts`
- WebSocket security via `verifyClient` in `server/ws.ts`

For iframe embedding of diffs.com, you'd need to add CSP headers allowing `https://diffs.com` as a frame source.

---

**Next Steps for Implementation:**
Would you like me to provide specific implementation guidance for any of these integration approaches? I can outline the exact code changes needed for:
1. Simple markdown links (zero code change, just documentation)
2. Embedded iframe viewer
3. Automatic diff URL generation from file changes
4. Custom diff viewer component

"use client";

/**
 * React hook that manages the WebSocket connection to the thos relay server.
 *
 * Supports multiple concurrent agents. Each agent has its own status,
 * message history, label, and tmux session name tracked in a Map keyed
 * by agent ID. The `activeAgentId` determines which agent's chat is shown.
 *
 * ## Connection lifecycle
 *
 * 1. Connect to `ws://<host>:9900/browser`.
 * 2. Server sends `agent_list` (sidebar metadata) + `task_list`. No
 *    message histories are sent eagerly — this keeps the initial
 *    payload small for fast loading on mobile networks.
 * 3. `initialLoadDone` becomes true after `agent_list` arrives.
 * 4. The first agent is auto-selected if nothing was selected.
 *
 * ## Lazy history loading
 *
 * Message histories are loaded on demand. When `activeAgentId` changes
 * and the agent hasn't been loaded yet, the hook sends
 * `{ type: "request_history", agentId }` and sets `historyLoading = true`.
 * When the server responds with `message_history`, the agent's messages
 * are populated and `historyLoading` becomes false.
 *
 * The `loadedAgents` Set tracks which agents have been fetched so that
 * switching back to a previously viewed agent is instant.
 *
 * ## Resilience features
 *
 * - Handles `message_history` replay from server on demand.
 * - Handles `cli_disconnected` / `cli_connected` events.
 * - Deduplicates messages using a per-agent processed count.
 * - Robust reconnection guard (clears previous timer before scheduling).
 * - Strict mode safe (closingRef prevents spurious reconnects on unmount).
 *
 * ## Logging
 *
 * All WS events are logged with the `[thos-ws]` prefix. Filter by this
 * in the browser console to debug connection and message delivery issues.
 */

# @pierre/diffs Overview

## What is it?
"@pierre/diffs is an open source diff and code rendering library. It's built on Shiki for syntax highlighting and theming, is super customizable, and comes packed with features."

## How it works
The library renders code differences using CSS Grid and Shadow DOM for performance. It supports multiple visualization styles including split (side-by-side) and stacked (unified) layouts with customizable diff indicators (bars, classic +/–, or none).

## Programmatic API
Yes, there's a programmatic approach. Users can "pass any two files in @pierre/diffs and get a diff between them," making it useful for comparing generative snapshots where linear history isn't available.

## Embedding
The site demonstrates embedded diffs with interactive features like line selection, custom annotations for comments, and accept/reject buttons for code review workflows.

## URL format & parameters
The page content doesn't specify a documented URL format or query parameters for creating diffs via links.

## Creating diffs
The site doesn't explain the creation process through the UI shown. Installation is via: `bun i @pierre/diffs` with full documentation available at `/docs`.

The library supports theming, custom fonts, line selection, annotations, and wrapping—all configurable per-component or globally.

# MultiFileDiff Component Props

## Import
Import from `'@pierre/diffs/react'`:
```javascript
import { MultiFileDiff } from '@pierre/diffs/react'
```

## Core Props

**oldFile** and **newFile** expect `FileContents` objects, which contain:
- `name`: filename string
- `contents`: file contents string

## FileContents Example
```javascript
const oldFile = {
  name: 'example.ts',
  contents: 'function greet(name: string) { ... }'
}
```

## Configuration Options

The component accepts shared props documented in the "Shared Props" section, including:

- **theme**: Theme name (e.g., `'pierre-dark'`)
- **diffStyle**: Display mode - `'split'` or unified format
- **lineAnnotations**: Add custom annotations to specific lines
- **enableLineSelection**: Allow users to select lines

Design an implementation plan for adding a diff viewer to the thos dashboard using the @pierre/diffs library.

## Context

thos is a visual orchestration layer for Claude Code. When Claude edits files, the tool_use content blocks contain `{ file_path, old_string, new_string }` for Edit tools and `{ file_path, content }` for Write tools. Currently these inputs are only visible as raw JSON in the debug view or as text in the control-request approval cards.

The goal: Show beautiful inline diffs in the chat view using `@pierre/diffs/react`'s `MultiFileDiff` component.

## Current Architecture

### Data Flow
1. Claude CLI sends NDJSON messages over WebSocket to `server/ws.ts`
2. Server relays to browser via `hooks/use-websocket.ts`
3. `relayChatMessage()` converts raw messages to `ChatMessage` objects
4. `condenseMessages()` groups consecutive tool-only messages
5. `chat.tsx` renders items as `Message`, `ControlRequest`, `UserQuestion`, or `CondensedToolGroup`

### Key Problem
`ToolCallInfo` only stores `{ name, toolUseId, resultPreview }` — the actual tool input data (file_path, old_string, new_string) is discarded during conversion. We need to preserve it.

### Types (lib/types.ts)
```ts
export interface ToolCallInfo {
  name: string;
  toolUseId?: string;
  resultPreview?: string;
}
```

### Tool Input Data Available
For Edit: `{ file_path: string, old_string: string, new_string: string }`
For Write: `{ file_path: string, content: string }`
For MultiEdit: `{ file_path: string, edits: Array<{old_string, new_string}> }`

### @pierre/diffs API
```tsx
import { MultiFileDiff } from '@pierre/diffs/react';
<MultiFileDiff 
  oldFile={{ name: 'file.ts', contents: '...' }}
  newFile={{ name: 'file.ts', contents: '...' }}
/>
```

## Files to Modify

1. **lib/types.ts** — Extend `ToolCallInfo` to include tool input data for file operations
2. **hooks/use-websocket.ts** — Preserve tool input data when building `ToolCallInfo` (lines 184-190)
3. **components/dashboard/condensed-tool-group.tsx** — Show diff viewer for Edit/Write tool calls
4. **components/dashboard/message.tsx** — Show diff viewer for non-condensed messages with tool calls
5. **package.json** — Add `@pierre/diffs` dependency

## Design Considerations

1. For Edit tools, we have both old_string and new_string — perfect for MultiFileDiff
2. For Write tools, we only have the new content — show as a "new file" diff (empty old file)
3. Diffs should be shown inline in the condensed tool group, collapsed by default
4. The diff viewer should respect the dark theme
5. Keep the implementation minimal — just render diffs where we already show tool call previews

# MultiFileDiff React Component API Documentation

## Import Path
```typescript
import { MultiFileDiff } from '@pierre/diffs/react'
```

## Component Purpose
The `MultiFileDiff` component renders a diff by accepting two file versions for comparison. It's one of four primary React components alongside `PatchDiff`, `FileDiff`, and `File`.

## Core Props

**File Objects:**
- `oldFile`: A `FileContents` object representing the original file
- `newFile`: A `FileContents` object representing the modified file

**FileContents Structure:**
Each file requires a filename and contents string. Per documentation: "Use it when rendering a file with the `<File>` component, or pass two of them as `oldFile` and `newFile` to diff components."

## Shared Configuration Props

The component accepts shared props documented under "Diff Options" including:

- **Styling**: Theme selection, CSS variable overrides
- **Annotations**: Line-level comments and metadata
- **Rendering Options**: Line diff type, diff display style
- **Interactivity**: Line selection, expand/collapse controls

## WorkerPoolContextProvider Setup

For offloading syntax highlighting to background threads:

```typescript
import { WorkerPoolContextProvider } from '@pierre/diffs/react'

<WorkerPoolContextProvider workerFactory={createWorker}>
  <MultiFileDiff oldFile={old} newFile={new} />
</WorkerPoolContextProvider>
```

The provider automatically manages worker pool lifecycle and is compatible with Next.js App Router (requires `'use client'` directive).

## Theme & Dark Mode

The component respects system theme preferences via shadow DOM CSS variables. Theme configuration occurs through props shared across all diff components, with support for custom Shiki themes via `registerCustomTheme()`.

## CSS Requirements

No explicit CSS imports needed—the component uses shadow DOM for style isolation, eliminating conflicts with page CSS.

# Diffs Library Documentation Summary

## Component Import Paths

**React Components** (from `@pierre/diffs/react`):
- `MultiFileDiff` - compares two file versions
- `PatchDiff` - renders from patch string
- `FileDiff` - renders pre-parsed `FileDiffMetadata`
- `File` - single code file without diff
- `WorkerPoolContextProvider` - worker pool setup

**Vanilla JS** (from `@pierre/diffs`):
- `FileDiff` class - compare files or render metadata
- `File` class - single file rendering

**Utilities** (from `@pierre/diffs`):
- `parseDiffFromFile` - generate metadata from two versions
- `parsePatchFiles` - parse unified diff strings
- `setLanguageOverride`, `registerCustomTheme`, `registerCustomLanguage`

**Worker Pool** (from `@pierre/diffs/worker`):
- `getOrCreateWorkerPoolSingleton` - Vanilla JS pool management
- `terminateWorkerPoolSingleton` - cleanup

**SSR** (from `@pierre/diffs/ssr`):
- `preloadMultiFileDiff`, `preloadFileDiff`, `preloadFile`, `preloadPatchDiff`, `preloadPatchFile`

## WorkerPoolContextProvider Configuration

Wrap component tree in React:
```
<WorkerPoolContextProvider workerFactory={yourWorkerFactory}>
  {children}
</WorkerPoolContextProvider>
```

Access via `useWorkerPool()` hook to call `setRenderOptions(options)` for dynamic theme/render option changes.

## FileContents Type

Object containing:
- `name` - filename string
- `contents` - file content string
- `cacheKey` (optional) - for render caching

## MultiFileDiff Props

Accepts `oldFile` and `newFile` (both `FileContents` objects), plus shared diff options for annotations, styling, and rendering configuration.

## FileDiff Props

Requires `fileDiffMetadata` (`FileDiffMetadata` structure with hunks and line counts), supports same shared annotation and styling props as `MultiFileDiff`.

## Required Imports

Core styling uses "shadow DOM APIs" for isolation—no separate stylesheet needed. Custom CSS variables override colors and layout via component props or global CSS.

## Next.js Configuration

Use `'use client'` directive for client components with workers. Server-side rendering via preload functions returns objects spreadable into client components: `<MultiFileDiff {...preloaded} />`.

## Theme Configuration

Specify `theme` prop (e.g., `'pierre-dark'`). Available: Pierre Light and Pierre Dark. "Register custom Shiki themes" using `registerCustomTheme`. Respects system preference via `enableSystem: true`.

## diffStyle Options

- `'split'` - side-by-side comparison
- `'unified'` - traditional unified format (inferred from documentation structure)

## Handling New Files

For files without old content, pass empty `FileContents` or rely on parsing utilities that handle creation detection in patch metadata.

# Changelog

## 2026-02-18 — SFX on everything

Every agent event now has a sound effect — different sound pools per tool type, plus sounds for session start, task completion, errors, and control requests. Random variant selection from each pool keeps it from getting monotonous. All sounds from soundcn (Kenney, CC0 licensed), embedded as base64 data URIs using the Web Audio API.

Sound mapping:
- **Write / Edit / MultiEdit** — impact-generic-light (percussive hit)
- **Read** — click (soft tap)
- **Bash** — computer-noise (electronic blip)
- **Grep / Glob / search tools** — tick (quick scan)
- **Session start** — begin / power-up
- **Task result (success)** — confirmation chime
- **Error** — error buzz
- **Control request / question** — question tone

### Changes

- **`lib/sfx.ts`** — New file. Central SFX module with sound pools mapped to tool names and event types. Exports `sfxTool()`, `sfxDone()`, `sfxError()`, `sfxQuestion()`, `sfxBegin()`. Each picks a random variant from the pool and plays via `playSound()` at calibrated volumes.

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Replaced old code-write-only SFX with full coverage. Imports from `lib/sfx.ts`. Triggers: `sfxTool()` on every relay with tool calls (first tool in message), `sfxDone()`/`sfxError()` on result messages, `sfxQuestion()` on control requests, `sfxBegin()` on session init, `sfxError()` on error messages.

- **`hooks/use-sound.ts`** — New file (installed via `npx shadcn add @soundcn/use-sound`). React hook for declarative sound playback using Web Audio API.

- **`lib/sound-engine.ts`** — New file (installed via soundcn). Shared AudioContext singleton, base64 decoding with buffer cache, and imperative `playSound()` function.

- **`lib/sound-types.ts`** — New file (installed via soundcn). TypeScript interfaces for `SoundAsset`, `UseSoundOptions`, and `UseSoundReturn`.

- **Sound assets** (all installed via `npx shadcn add @soundcn/...`):
  - `lib/impact-generic-light-{000..004}.ts` — 5 impact sounds

# Changelog

## 2026-02-18 — SFX on everything

Every agent event now has a sound effect — different sound pools per tool type, plus sounds for session start, task completion, errors, and control requests. Random variant selection from each pool keeps it from getting monotonous. All sounds from soundcn (Kenney, CC0 licensed), embedded as base64 data URIs using the Web Audio API.

Sound mapping:
- **Write / Edit / MultiEdit** — impact-generic-light (percussive hit)
- **Read** — click (soft tap)
- **Bash** — computer-noise (electronic blip)
- **Grep / Glob / search tools** — tick (quick scan)
- **Session start** — begin / power-up
- **Task result (success)** — confirmation chime
- **Error** — error buzz
- **Control request / question** — question tone

### Changes

- **`lib/sfx.ts`** — New file. Central SFX module with sound pools mapped to tool names and event types. Exports `sfxTool()`, `sfxDone()`, `sfxError()`, `sfxQuestion()`, `sfxBegin()`. Each picks a random variant from the pool and plays via `playSound()` at calibrated volumes.

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Replaced old code-write-only SFX with full coverage. Imports from `lib/sfx.ts`. Triggers: `sfxTool()` on every relay with tool calls (first tool in message), `sfxDone()`/`sfxError()` on result messages, `sfxQuestion()` on control requests, `sfxBegin()` on session init, `sfxError()` on error messages.

- **`hooks/use-sound.ts`** — New file (installed via `npx shadcn add @soundcn/use-sound`). React hook for declarative sound playback using Web Audio API.

- **`lib/sound-engine.ts`** — New file (installed via soundcn). Shared AudioContext singleton, base64 decoding with buffer cache, and imperative `playSound()` function.

- **`lib/sound-types.ts`** — New file (installed via soundcn). TypeScript interfaces for `SoundAsset`, `UseSoundOptions`, and `UseSoundReturn`.

- **Sound assets** (all installed via `npx shadcn add @soundcn/...`):
  - `lib/impact-generic-light-{000..004}.ts` — 5 impact sounds
  - `lib/click-{soft,001..004}.ts` — 5 click sounds
  - `lib/computer-noise-{000..003}.ts` — 4 computer noise sounds
  - `lib/tick-{001,002,004}.ts` — 3 tick sounds
  - `lib/confirmation-{001..004}.ts` — 4 confirmation sounds
  - `lib/error-{001..003}.ts` — 3 error sounds
  - `lib/question-{001..003}.ts` — 3 question sounds
  - `lib/begin.ts`, `lib/power-up-1.ts` — 2 session start sounds

## 2026-02-18 — Workspaces with server-side folder browser

Added workspaces to group agents and tasks by project directory. Each workspace has a name and an absolute `cwd` path. Agents spawned within a workspace start their tmux session in that directory. The sidebar workspace switcher filters agents and tasks per-workspace, or shows everything in "All Workspaces" mode.

Creating a workspace uses a server-side folder browser — the browser sends `browse_directory` messages over WebSocket and the server responds with directory listings. This works over Tailscale since it doesn't rely on native file dialogs.

### Changes

- **`lib/types.ts`** — Added `Workspace` and `DirectoryEntry` interfaces. Added `workspaceId` to `AgentInfo`, `Task`, and `BrowserSpawn`. Added browser messages (`set_workspace`, `create_workspace`, `rename_workspace`, `delete_workspace`, `browse_directory`) and server messages (`workspace_list`, `directory_listing`). Also fixed pre-existing build errors: added `total_cost_usd` to `ClaudeResult`, added `"icebox"` to `TaskStatus`.

- **`server/workspace-store.ts`** — New file. JSON persistence for workspaces at `.thos/workspaces.json` with `loadAll()` and `saveSync()`.

- **`server/session-store.ts`** — Added `workspaceId: string | null` to `PersistedAgent.state`.

- **`server/ws.ts`** — Added `WorkspaceStore`, workspace state maps, and per-browser workspace scoping (`browserWorkspaceScope`). `buildAgentList()` and `buildTaskList()` now accept optional workspace filter. `broadcastAgentList()` and `broadcastTaskList()` send scoped data per-browser. `spawnClaude()` accepts `workspaceId` and starts tmux in the workspace's cwd. Added handlers for `set_workspace`, `create_workspace`, `rename_workspace`, `delete_workspace`, and `browse_directory`. Workspace cleanup on browser disconnect and persistence on shutdown. Also fixed pre-existing implicit `any` type on `verifyClient`.

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Added workspace state (`workspaces`, `activeWorkspaceId`, `directoryListing`), handlers for `workspace_list` and `directory_listing` messages, and action functions (`setActiveWorkspaceId`, `createWorkspace`, `renameWorkspace`, `deleteWorkspace`, `browseDirectory`).

- **`components/dashboard/workspace-switcher.tsx`** — New component. Dropdown in the sidebar header showing the active workspace name and cwd. Lists all workspaces with inline rename and delete actions. "Open Folder..." triggers the folder browser modal.

- **`components/dashboard/folder-browser.tsx`** — New component. Modal dialog for browsing the server's filesystem. Shows breadcrumb navigation, directory listing (folders only, dotfiles hidden), parent directory navigation, and a name input that auto-fills with the directory basename.

- **`components/dashboard/agent-sidebar.tsx`** — Replaced the branding header with `WorkspaceSwitcher`. Added workspace props.

- **`app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — Wired workspace values from the hook to the sidebar and folder browser. Added `FolderBrowser` modal state.

- **`components/dashboard/task-card.tsx`** — Added `icebox` to status color, label, and cycle maps (pre-existing build fix).

- **`middleware.ts`** — Fixed `req.ip` type error for Next.js 16 compatibility.

## 2026-02-18 — Fix status message duplication on page reload

Reloading the browser caused "Done — X turns" and "Session started" status messages to stack up, appearing dozens of times. The server's message deduplication only covered `assistant` and `user` message types — `system/init` and `result` messages were always appended to history, so each reload replayed all of them.

### Changes

- **`server/ws.ts`** — Extended `getRelayMessageId()` to return stable dedup keys for `system/init` (keyed by `init:<session_id>`) and `result` (keyed by `result:<session_id>`) messages, so they replace rather than append in `messageHistory`.

## 2026-02-18 — Slash command autocomplete

Added a slash command autocomplete menu to the chat input. When the user types `/` as the first character, a dropdown appears above the input showing matching Claude Code commands. Commands are sent as text to the CLI which handles them natively; `/clear` is handled client-side.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/slash-command-menu.tsx`** — New component with a registry of 12 slash commands (commit, review-pr, clear, compact, cost, doctor, init, config, memory, status, model, help), each with an icon and description. Exports `filterCommands()` for case-insensitive substring matching and `SlashCommandMenu` dropdown component. Uses `onMouseDown` with `preventDefault` to prevent input blur on click.

- **`components/dashboard/chat.tsx`** — Integrated slash command detection: typing `/` triggers the menu, arrow keys navigate, Enter selects, Tab autocompletes the command name, Escape dismisses. Client-side commands (like `/clear`) call the appropriate handler directly; all others are sent as regular messages to the CLI. Added `onClearHistory` prop for the `/clear` command.

- **`app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — Wired `onClearHistory` callback to call `clearHistory(activeAgentId)` from the WebSocket hook.

## 2026-02-17 — Tool call result previews

Condensed tool groups showed which tools were called but not their results. Now each tool call displays a truncated one-line preview of its result inline, giving context without expanding the group. Previews show when collapsed; expanding still reveals the full messages.

### Changes

- **`lib/types.ts`** — Added optional `resultPreview` field to `ToolCallInfo`.

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — When building `ToolCallInfo` from assistant content blocks, pair each `tool_use` with its corresponding `tool_result` (matched by `tool_use_id`) and extract a truncated first-line preview (max 120 chars).

- **`components/dashboard/condensed-tool-group.tsx`** — When collapsed, render per-tool-call rows with a colored dot, tool name, and truncated result preview. Added color mapping for common tool names.

## 2026-02-17 — Kanban board for tasks

Replaced the task panel with a dual-mode view: a compact list (right sidebar, w-80) and a full-width kanban board. Toggle between modes via the header button. Added an Icebox column for parking ideas.

**List mode** — right sidebar alongside the chat, grouped by status (In Progress, Todo, Icebox, Done). Icebox and Done are collapsible. Cards are draggable between groups.

**Board mode** — replaces the chat area with four columns (Icebox, Todo, In Progress, Done). Cards drag between columns. Horizontally scrollable with min-width per column.

### Changes

- **`lib/types.ts`** — Added `"icebox"` to `TaskStatus` union for parking ideas/later items.

- **`components/dashboard/kanban-board.tsx`** — Unified `TaskPanel` component with list/board toggle. List mode renders grouped task sections with collapsible Icebox and Done. Board mode renders four kanban columns. Both modes support drag-and-drop between groups/columns. Exports `TaskViewMode` type.

- **`components/dashboard/task-card.tsx`** — Added icebox to status color map (purple), label map, and status cycling (icebox → todo).

- **`app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — Task view state is now `"hidden" | "list" | "board"`. List mode shows task panel as a right sidebar (w-80) alongside the chat. Board mode hides chat and gives the panel full width. The status bar toggle opens list mode; switching to board happens from within the panel header.

- **`components/dashboard/task-panel.tsx`** — Deleted. Replaced by unified `TaskPanel` in kanban-board.tsx.

## 2026-02-17 — Connection status toast

WebSocket reconnection happened silently. Added brief toast notifications when the connection drops ("Connection lost") and restores ("Reconnected") to build trust that the system is recovering. Toasts do not fire on the initial page load.

### Changes

- **`package.json`** — Added `sonner` for toast notifications.

- **`components/ui/sonner.tsx`** — New Toaster wrapper component with dark theme and monospace font.

- **`app/dashboard/page.tsx`** — Added `useEffect` watching `connected` state with a `hasConnectedRef` guard to skip the initial connection. Shows `toast.error` on disconnect and `toast.success` on reconnect. Renders `<Toaster />` in the page.

## 2026-02-17 — Fix duplicate "Session started" on follow-up messages

Sending a follow-up message to a running agent would re-display "Session started — model: ..., cwd: ..." in the chat. The CLI re-sends `system/init` on every turn, and the server was relaying and storing all of them.

### Changes

- **`server/ws.ts`** — Only relay the first `system/init` message per agent. Subsequent init messages (re-sent by CLI on each turn) are still used to update `sessionId` and status, but are no longer recorded in history or broadcast to browsers.

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Changed `system/init` ChatMessage ID from `nextId()` (random) to `dedup-init-{session_id}` (stable) as a belt-and-suspenders safeguard.

## 2026-02-17 — Fix message duplication in chat

Claude CLI sends cumulative NDJSON snapshots for assistant messages (each line is a complete snapshot of the message so far). The server correctly deduplicates these in stored history, but the browser received every snapshot as a live relay and appended each one as a new ChatMessage, causing messages to appear 2-4x in the chat window. Also caused React duplicate key warnings.

### Changes

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Added `getRelayDedupKey()` to extract stable message IDs from relay messages (assistant `message.id`, user `uuid`). Changed `relayChatMessage()` to use these stable IDs (prefixed with `dedup-`) instead of generating new random IDs for each snapshot. Updated the relay handler to replace existing ChatMessages with the same dedup ID instead of appending. Added `findLastRawIndex()` helper to also deduplicate raw messages in the debug view.

## 2026-02-17 — Message timestamps

Messages had no timestamps, making it hard to track conversation flow. Added relative timestamps ("just now", "2m ago", "1h ago") below each user and assistant message bubble, with absolute time shown on hover via the native tooltip.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/message.tsx`** — Added `formatRelativeTime()` utility and `RelativeTime` component that auto-updates every 30s. Renders below each user/assistant bubble as a small muted label. Uses `<time>` element with `title` for hover-to-see-absolute-time and `dateTime` for accessibility.

## 2026-02-17 — Agent cost/duration summary

Added a compact summary bar at the top of the chat area showing total cost, duration, turn count, and token usage for the active agent. Stats are extracted from `result` messages in the raw NDJSON stream.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/agent-summary.tsx`** — New component that scans raw Claude messages for `result` entries and displays total cost (last result's cumulative `total_cost_usd`), total duration (summed `duration_ms`), total turns (summed `num_turns`), and total token usage (summed from each result's `usage` object) in a slim bar with icons. Hovering the token count shows a breakdown of input, output, cache read, and cache write tokens. Only renders when result data is available.

- **`components/dashboard/chat.tsx`** — Added `AgentSummary` between the status bar and the scrollable message area.

- **`lib/types.ts`** — Added `total_cost_usd` field to `ClaudeResult` (the actual field name used by the CLI, alongside the existing `cost_usd`).

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Updated result summary text to prefer `total_cost_usd` over `cost_usd`.

## 2026-02-17 — Empty state for chat area

When no agent is selected, the chat area showed only a single line of text. Replaced it with a proper empty state featuring a terminal icon, descriptive copy, and quick-reference cards for Chat and Tasks features.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/chat.tsx`** — Replaced the minimal "Type a prompt to spawn a Claude agent" text with a centered empty state panel showing a terminal icon, heading, description, and two feature hint cards (Chat, Tasks). Added `Terminal`, `MessageSquare`, and `ListTodo` icon imports from lucide-react.

## 2026-02-17 — Copy message button

No way to copy a message's content. A small copy icon on hover makes it easy.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/message.tsx`** — Added a `CopyButton` component that appears in the top-right corner of user and assistant message bubbles on hover. Uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText` and shows a checkmark for 1.5s after copying. The message bubble gets `group relative` classes to support the hover reveal.

## 2026-02-17 — Archive agent when task marked as complete

When a task with a linked agent was marked as "done", the agent kept running. Now the server automatically stops (archives) the linked agent when the task status is set to "done".

### Changes

- **`server/ws.ts`** — In the `update_task` handler, after persisting and broadcasting the task update, check if the task was marked "done" and has a linked `agentId`. If so, call `stopAgent()` to kill the tmux session and set the agent to "done" status.

## 2026-02-17 — Edit todo functionality

Task editing was only accessible via a hidden double-click gesture on the title, making it hard to discover.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/task-card.tsx`** — Added explicit edit button (pencil icon) to the task card hover actions, visible alongside delegate and delete buttons. Edit mode now includes an inline priority selector so all task fields (title, description, priority) can be edited in one pass. Double-click on title still works as a shortcut. All edit state (title, description, priority) is properly initialized when entering edit mode from either entry point.

## 2026-02-17 — Improved tool approval window

The tool approval card was too small (`max-w-lg`) and showed raw JSON, making it hard to review tool inputs before approving.

### Changes

- **`components/dashboard/control-request.tsx`** — Redesigned the tool approval card:
  - Wider layout (`max-w-2xl`)
  - Header row with shield icon, formatted tool name, and full name for namespaced tools
  - Individual input parameters displayed as labeled fields instead of raw JSON dump
  - Long string values (commands, file contents) render in scrollable code blocks
  - Short strings render as inline `<code>` elements
  - Allow/Deny buttons now have icons (Check/X) and Deny uses `outline` variant instead of `destructive`
  - Resolved state shows a colored pill badge ("Allowed" / "Denied") instead of generic "Resolved" text
  - Dimmed styling when resolved to reduce visual noise
  - Shows `description` field from the protocol when available

- **`lib/types.ts`** — Added optional `description` field to `ChatMessage.controlRequest` type.

- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Pass through `description` from `ClaudeControlRequest` to the `ChatMessage` control request payload.

## 2026-02-17 — Fix initial message missing from chat history

When spawning a new agent, the initial user prompt was sent to the CLI but never recorded in `messageHistory` or relayed to the browser. This meant the first message never appeared in the chat view, and was also missing after page reloads.

### Changes

- **`server/ws.ts`** — Added `recordAndSend()` calls in both prompt delivery paths (direct CLI connect and `hook_response` fallback) so the initial user message is stored in history and broadcast to browsers, matching the behavior of follow-up `send_message` handling.

## 2026-02-16 — Markdown rendering

**Task:** [#58300471] Markdown rendering

Assistant messages were rendered as plain text, so markdown output from Claude (code blocks, headers, lists, bold, tables) showed as raw syntax.

### Changes

- **`package.json`** — Added `react-markdown` (v10.1.0) and `remark-gfm` (v4.0.1) for markdown parsing with GitHub Flavored Markdown support (tables, strikethrough, task lists, autolinks).

- **`components/dashboard/message.tsx`** — Assistant messages now render through `<Markdown remarkPlugins={[remarkGfm]}>` instead of plain text. User messages remain plain text with `whitespace-pre-wrap`. System messages unchanged.

- **`app/globals.css`** — Added `.prose-msg` class with styles for all markdown elements:
  - Headings (h1–h4), bold/strong
  - Inline code (subtle background) and fenced code blocks (darker background, horizontal scroll)
  - Ordered and unordered lists with nested list support
  - Blockquotes (left border accent, muted color)
  - Links (primary color, underlined)
  - Tables (collapsed borders, header background)
  - Horizontal rules, images
  - Light theme overrides for backgrounds and borders

# Diffs Sidebar Panel — Implementation Plan

## Context

Inline diffs were just added to the chat view (condensed tool groups + standalone messages). Now we want to collect all file diffs from the active session into a dedicated sidebar panel — similar to how the task panel works. This gives a single view of every file change the agent has made.

## Approach

Follow the exact same pattern as the task panel: state toggle in `page.tsx`, button in `StatusBar`, conditional drawer JSX, new `DiffsPanel` component. The diff data is derived from `activeMessages` via `useMemo` — no hook or server changes needed.

## Changes

### 1. `components/dashboard/diffs-panel.tsx` (new file)

New panel component receiving `ChatMessage[]` as prop. Internally:
- `useMemo` to extract all `ToolCallInfo` with `input` from messages where `name` is Edit/Write/MultiEdit
- Group by file path (most recent edit per file at top, or chronological list)
- Render each with `DiffViewer` component (already exists)
- Header with "Diffs" title, count badge, and close button (matching TaskPanel header pattern)
- Scrollable content area

### 2. `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx`

Add a diffs toggle button (using `GitCompareArrows` or `FileDiff` icon from lucide) next to the task toggle button. New props: `showDiffs?: boolean`, `onToggleDiffs?: () => void`.

### 3. `app/dashboard/page.tsx`

- Add `showDiffs` state: `useState(false)`
- Pass `activeMessages` and toggle to `DiffsPanel`
- Add panel drawer JSX following task panel pattern (right side, `w-96`, `border-l`)
- Pass `showDiffs` / `onToggleDiffs` through `Chat` → `StatusBar`
- When both tasks and diffs are open, only show one (diffs takes priority, or they stack)

### 4. `components/dashboard/chat.tsx`

Thread `showDiffs` / `onToggleDiffs` props through to `StatusBar`.

## Verification

1. `pnpm build` — no type errors
2. `pnpm dev` — toggle diffs panel via status bar button
3. Spawn agent that edits files → diffs appear in panel grouped by file
4. Panel scrolls, close button works, mobile backdrop works

Inline diffs were just added to the chat view (condensed tool groups + standalone messages). Now we want to collect all file diffs from the active session into a dedicated sidebar panel — similar to how the task panel works. This gives a single view of every file change the agent has made.

## Approach

Follow the exact same pattern as the task panel: state toggle in `page.tsx`, button in `StatusBar`, conditional drawer JSX, new `DiffsPanel` component. The diff data is derived from `activeMessages` via `useMemo` — no hook or server changes needed.

## Changes

### 1. `components/dashboard/diffs-panel.tsx` (new file)

New panel component receiving `ChatMessage[]` as prop. Internally:
- `useMemo` to extract all `ToolCallInfo` with `input` from messages where `name` is Edit/Write/MultiEdit
- Group by file path (most recent edit per file at top, or chronological list)
- Render each with `DiffViewer` component (already exists)
- Header with "Diffs" title, count badge, and close button (matching TaskPanel header pattern)
- Scrollable content area

### 2. `components/dashboard/status-bar.tsx`

Add a diffs toggle button (using `GitCompareArrows` or `FileDiff` icon from lucide) next to the task toggle button. New props: `showDiffs?: boolean`, `onToggleDiffs?: () => void`.

### 3. `app/dashboard/page.tsx`

- Add `showDiffs` state: `useState(false)`
- Pass `activeMessages` and toggle to `DiffsPanel`
- Add panel drawer JSX following task panel pattern (right side, `w-96`, `border-l`)
- Pass `showDiffs` / `onToggleDiffs` through `Chat` → `StatusBar`
- When both tasks and diffs are open, only show one (diffs takes priority, or they stack)

### 4. `components/dashboard/chat.tsx`

Thread `showDiffs` / `onToggleDiffs` props through to `StatusBar`.

## Verification

1. `pnpm build` — no type errors
2. `pnpm dev` — toggle diffs panel via status bar button
3. Spawn agent that edits files → diffs appear in panel grouped by file
4. Panel scrolls, close button works, mobile backdrop works

# Diff Viewer — Implementation Plan

## Context

When Claude edits files, the tool_use blocks contain `{ file_path, old_string, new_string }` but this data is discarded during message conversion — only tool name and a truncated result preview are kept. The goal is to render inline diffs in the chat view using `@pierre/diffs/react`'s `MultiFileDiff` component.

## Changes

### 1. Install `@pierre/diffs`

```
pnpm add @pierre/diffs
```

### 2. Extend `ToolCallInfo` — `lib/types.ts`

Add optional `input` field to carry tool input data for file-modifying tools:

```ts
export interface ToolCallInfo {
  name: string;
  toolUseId?: string;
  resultPreview?: string;
  input?: Record<string, unknown>;  // NEW
}
```

### 3. Preserve tool input in `relayChatMessage()` — `hooks/use-websocket.ts`

Lines 184-190: When building `ToolCallInfo` objects, preserve the `input` for Edit/Write/MultiEdit tools (reuse the existing `CODE_UPDATE_TOOLS` set at line 83).

### 4. Create `DiffViewer` component — `components/dashboard/diff-viewer.tsx` (new file)

- Accepts a `ToolCallInfo` prop
- Extracts `file_path`, `old_string`, `new_string` from input based on tool name
- Renders `<MultiFileDiff oldFile={...} newFile={...} />` from `@pierre/diffs/react`
- Handles Edit (old→new), Write (empty→content), MultiEdit (concatenated hunks)
- Skips rendering if content exceeds 100KB

### 5. Integrate into condensed tool groups — `components/dashboard/condensed-tool-group.tsx`

- Add per-tool-call expandable diff toggle in collapsed view
- Show basename of file path instead of result preview for diff-capable tools
- Click to expand/collapse individual diffs inline

### 6. Integrate into standalone messages — `components/dashboard/message.tsx`

- For assistant messages with file-modifying tool calls, render `DiffViewer` inline below the message content

### 7. Update `CHANGELOG.md`

## Verification

1. Run `pnpm dev`
2. Spawn a Claude agent that edits a file (e.g. "add a comment to package.json")
3. Verify the diff renders inline in the condensed tool group
4. Click to expand/collapse individual diffs
5. Verify Write tool calls show as new-file diffs
6. Check that non-diff tools (Read, Bash, Grep) still show result previews as before

# Changelog

## 2026-02-18 — Inline diff viewer

File diffs now render inline in the chat view using `@pierre/diffs`. When Claude edits or writes files, the old/new content is shown as a syntax-highlighted diff. In condensed tool groups, click a file name to expand the diff. Standalone messages show diffs automatically.

### Changes

- **`@pierre/diffs`** — Added as dependency for diff rendering (`MultiFileDiff` component)
- **`lib/types.ts`** — Added optional `input` field to `ToolCallInfo` to carry tool input data for Edit/Write/MultiEdit
- **`hooks/use-websocket.ts`** — Preserve tool input in `relayChatMessage()` for diff-capable tools
- **`components/dashboard/diff-viewer.tsx`** — New component wrapping `MultiFileDiff`, handles Edit (old→new), Write (empty→new), and MultiEdit (concatenated hunks). Skips diffs over 100KB.
- **`components/dashboard/condensed-tool-group.tsx`** — Per-tool-call expandable diffs in collapsed view, shows file basename
- **`components/dashboard/message.tsx`** — Inline diffs for standalone assistant messages with file-modifying tool calls
